prs.title: Check package reachability before using exports in declarations
prs.author: Andarist
prs.body:
fixes https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/issues/64590

The issue was causedd by an early return~, the code sequence was roughly was:

1. Inspect package.json.
2. If exports supplies a specifier, return it immediately.
3. Check whether the importing file can reach that node_modules directory.

So the step 2 bypassed the step 3's validation~ entirely. The fix simply relies on reordering the steps listed above. It now validates the reachability before checking if the exports have the specifier.

prs.title: Fix invalid decorator examples in lib.decorators.d.ts
prs.author: wfatih
prs.body:
Fixes #54338
Fixes #54099

### Problem

Both `@example` blocks in `lib.decorators.d.ts` reference types that do not exist in any lib file:

* `ClassDecoratorContext.addInitializer` annotates the returned decorator as `ClassDecoratorFunction`
* `ClassMethodDecoratorContext.addInitializer` annotates `bound` as `ClassMethodDecoratorFunction`

Neither name is declared anywhere in the repository (`git grep` finds only these two comments), so both snippets fail with `Cannot find name '...'`. The second snippet is additionally not parseable — `const bound: ClassMethodDecoratorFunction = (value, context) { ... }` is missing the `=>` — so it cannot be pasted into an editor as-is.

### Change

Both snippets are rewritten in terms of the context types this file actually declares:

* the class-decorator example is now a decorator factory generic over `Class extends CustomElementConstructor`, with the element class extending `HTMLElement` so `customElements.define(name, this)` is valid;
* the `bound` example is now a generic function declaration taking `value: Value` and `context: ClassMethodDecoratorContext<This, Value>`, with the dynamic member access done through an explicit `Record<PropertyKey, any>` view of `this`.

Behaviour of the examples is unchanged; only the annotations and the syntax error are fixed.

prs.title: Fix nil panic when stripInternal elides type alias RHS
prs.author: andre-fajar-n
prs.body:
Fixes #64667
  ## Analysis
  With `--declaration --stripInternal`, `@internal` on a type-alias RHS can be stripped by `visitDeclarationSubtree`, leaving a nil
  `Type` on the alias:
  ```ts
  interface Foo {}
  export type T =
      /** @internal */
      Foo;
  ```
  Declaration emit then called `ast.GetTypeNodePrecedence` with nil from `emitTypeAliasDeclaration` → `emitTypeNode`, causing:
  `panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference`
  Index signatures already fall back to `any` when the visited type is nil; type aliases did not.
  ## Fix
  In `transformTypeAliasDeclaration`, if `Visit(input.Type)` returns nil, substitute `any` (same pattern as
  `transformIndexSignatureDeclaration`). Added `declarationEmitStripInternalTypeAliasRHS.ts` and baselines.
  Alternate considered: nil-guard only in `emitTypeNode` / `GetTypeNodePrecedence`. That would avoid the crash but could emit an
  incomplete alias; transforming to `any` matches existing stripInternal declaration behavior.
  ## AI Assistance
  This PR was authored with AI assistance (Cursor); I have reviewed and understand the changes.

prs.title: Match Strada and don't resolve imports of ambient modules declared in the same file
prs.author: Andarist
prs.body:
fixes https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/issues/64486

It might be surprising that this issue resolves the referenced issue... so the story goes like this:
1. `IntersectionObserver` gets passed to `DeepPartial`
2. `IntersectionObserver` references `Element`, `Document`, `Window`, `typeof globalThis`
3. `@types/lodash` "installs" itself a a global UMD variable through `export as namespace _`
4. So `DeepPartial` walks through the whole Lodash API and that fans out to a lot of instantiations

This PR avoids this because the repro's `lodash-isempty.d.ts` contains `declare module 'lodash/isEmpty' { import _isEmpty from 'lodash/isEmpty'; ... }`. Strada treats that inner import as referring to the locally declared ambient module and doesn't resolve it. But Corsa resolved it to `@types/lodash/isEmpty.d.ts`, pulling all of `@types/lodash` into the program.

prs.title: [api] Leave a config out of its own extended source files
prs.author: cplieger
prs.body:
When an opened config's `extends` chain cycles back to it, `parseConfig` lists the config in its own `ExtendedSourceFiles`. It gets there through the edge that closes the cycle, or through a cached extended config whose list was built while another project was opened. The project registry walks that list in `updateExtendingConfigs` while it holds the config's own entry lock, so `LoadOrStore` waits on that lock and `createSnapshot` never returns.

**Impact:** one circular `extends` in a repository makes `createSnapshot` hang with no error, where `tsc -p` reports TS18000 and exits 2 at once, so an analyzer on the API stalls on that repository instead of reporting what is wrong with it.

`parseConfig` now skips the config's own path when it assembles `ExtendedSourceFiles`, compared by `PathKey` as the circularity check does. Every other config in the chain stays in the list, so watching and cache invalidation see the same dependencies, and TS18000 is reported as before. Strada also lists the config in this case, but nothing there walks the list under that config's lock.

`TestOpenProjectsWithCircularExtendsReportCircularity` opens `p1` and then `p2` in one session. Both extend `shared/base.json`, which extends `p2`, so `p2` reaches itself through the edge that closes the cycle and through the `base.json` entry cached while `p1` was opened.
